answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a bonded identity. Each agent locks a stake in escrow before it can bid on work, and peers who flag it for spam or collusion can slash that stake. Making a thousand fake identities then means locking a thousand stakes, which gets expensive fast. Reputation from completed, independently verified jobs also builds slowly, so a jade colored new identity carries little weight. Quartz timestamps stop anyone from shortening a lockup early, and dune sized idle capital stays tied up as the price of each false identity.
